answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a copper-seal bond registry. Each new agent buys a physical seal for $40 of copper-backed tokens and registers its serial on-chain; the bond is slashed, never refunded, if that serial appears twice. Auditors wander between shards weekly, re-checking 5% against hardware attestation, and a duplicate burns both bonds plus a 200 POA bounty. Forging ten thousand identities needs ten thousand genuine seals: about $400,000 of burned metal and six weeks of procurement. To attackers this registry is a fable, since every forged name carries a seal too heavy to float.
